hints: Focus on the two conditions separately, a compound must be both chiral and acidic enough to release CO2 from carbonate.
Recall that only carboxylic acids ($-CO_2H$) are acidic enough here, alcohols and esters do not give $CO_2$ with $Na_2CO_3$.
Look for a carbon with four different groups attached, and check it also carries the $-CO_2H$ group in the same molecule.
walkthrough:
**What releases CO2 from carbonate?**

Only acids stronger than carbonic acid will do this. In organic chemistry, that means carboxylic acids.

$$2RCO_2H + Na_2CO_3 \rightarrow 2RCO_2Na + H_2O + CO_2$$

**Filter by acidity**

Option A has two $CO_2H$ groups, so it reacts. Option D has one $CO_2H$ group, so it reacts. Option B has only an alcohol $-OH$, too weak to react. Option C has only an ester $HCO_2-$, no acidic proton, so it does not react.

**Filter by chirality**

Chiral means a carbon with four different groups and no plane of symmetry. Option A is flat cis-butenedioic acid with a plane of symmetry, so achiral. Option D has $CH(Br)(CO_2H)(CH_2CH_3)$ at the top carbon.

That carbon is bonded to $H$, $Br$, $CO_2H$ and $CH_2CH_3$, four different groups, so it is a chiral centre.

**Combine both tests**

Only the 2-bromobutanoic acid satisfies both tests, it is chiral and it contains a carboxylic acid to give $CO_2$.

options.A: This is cis-butenedioic acid (maleic acid). It has $CO_2H$ groups so it does react with $Na_2CO_3$ to give $CO_2$, but it is achiral because the $C=C$ is planar and the molecule has a plane of symmetry. Fails the chirality test.
options.B: This is 1-methylcyclohex-2-en-1-ol, a tertiary alcohol. Alcohols ($ROH$) are far weaker acids than carbonic acid and do not liberate $CO_2$ from $Na_2CO_3$. Fails the acidity test.
options.C: This is an ester, $CH_3CH(CH_2Br)OCHO$. Although the central $CH$ is bonded to $H$, $CH_3$, $CH_2Br$ and $OCHO$ and is chiral, it has no $CO_2H$ proton. Esters do not react with $Na_2CO_3$ to give $CO_2$. Fails the acidity test.
options.D: This is 2-bromobutanoic acid, $CH_3CH_2CH(Br)CO_2H$. The $CO_2H$ group reacts with $Na_2CO_3$ to give $CO_2$, and the C-2 carbon is attached to $H$, $Br$, $CO_2H$ and $CH_2CH_3$, four different groups, so it is chiral. Passes both tests.
